The authors introduce TALL-masks, a method that identifies per-task supports from task vectors and shows that applying these masks to the merged multi-task vector recovers >99% of single-task accuracy, and they analyze mask intersections to identify “selfish” and “catastrophic” weights that harm fusion; based on this they propose Consensus Merging, which removes such detrimental weights to improve merging quality. Empirically across vision and NLP benchmarks with up to 20 tasks, Consensus Merging consistently boosts existing merging methods and enables a compression scheme that reduces storage dramatically (e.g., from 57GB to 8.2GB) while preserving ~99.7% performance.

result.text: The paper tackles federated learning under statistical heterogeneity, where differing local data distributions slow convergence and complicate model aggregation. Its key insight is to leverage neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory to exchange richer, sample-wise Jacobian information instead of conventional model weights or gradients, enabling the server to treat the federated system as a kernel regression problem that better captures local function behavior. Concretely, participants upload per-sample Jacobian matrices, the server builds an empirical NTK matrix and computes global updates (effectively performing a kernelized update rather than explicit gradient descent), and a communication-efficient, privacy-enhanced variant reduces upload cost and exposure. result.text: LongVideoBench addresses the lack of public benchmarks for evaluating large multimodal models (LMMs) on long, interleaved video-language inputs by introducing a question-answering dataset that tests long-term multimodal understanding up to hour-long videos. result.text: The paper addresses the difficulty of enforcing principled trust-region constraints in deep reinforcement learning, where popular methods like TRPO and PPO rely on approximations that can violate constraints, hamper exploration, and be sensitive to implementation details. Its key insight is that trust regions can be enforced exactly and efficiently for deep Gaussian policies by inserting differentiable neural network layers that project policy parameters into per-state trust regions via closed-form solutions. The method derives analytic projection operators for Gaussian policies under multiple divergence metrics (KL divergence, Wasserstein L2, and Frobenius norm) and integrates these layers into standard learning pipelines so that policy outputs are projected during forward passes and remain end-to-end differentiable; experiments show comparable or improved performance and robustness relative to existing approaches while reducing sensitivity to implementation choices.

result.text: This paper addresses the scalability gap in Neural Processes (NPs), where Transformer-based NPs deliver strong predictive performance but incur quadratic cost in the number of context points, while existing sub-quadratic alternatives underperform. The key insight is to compress the context set into a constant, adjustable number of latent vectors that act as an information bottleneck, enabling self-attention among latents and multiple cross-attentions between targets and latents to recover higher-order context information without depending on context size. The proposed Latent Bottlenecked Attentive Neural Processes (LBANPs) therefore achieve sub-quadratic querying complexity by encoding contexts into fixed-size latents, applying self- and cross-attention to propagate and retrieve relevant summaries, and tuning the number of latents to trade off computation and accuracy. Empirically, LBANPs match or approach state-of-the-art performance on meta-regression, image completion, and contextual bandits while scaling to larger datasets than prior attention-based NPs.

result.text: The paper addresses the limited universality of ImageNet-pretrained encoders for open-world image retrieval by creating a more diverse training signal from large-scale web data while keeping representations compact and robust to noisy pseudo-labels. The key insight is to form a million pseudo-classes from LAION400M using joint CLIP text–image features and then mitigate inevitable inter-class confusion and noisy clustering by injecting stochasticity along both class and feature axes during training. Concretely, Unicom constructs a margin-based softmax that computes logits against randomly sampled subsets of class prototypes and measures similarity using randomly sampled feature dimensions of the prototype matrix, which together reduce label conflict and encourage low-dimensional, discriminative embeddings. This dual random partial-selection scheme yields compact, conflict-robust image descriptors that substantially improve retrieval performance over prior unsupervised and supervised methods.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of decoding natural images from noisy, non-invasive EEG recordings to enable object recognition directly from brain signals. Its key insight is that self-supervised contrastive learning can align representations learned from paired image stimuli and EEG responses, allowing useful image features to be inferred from EEG despite low signal-to-noise ratios. The method uses separate image and EEG encoders trained with a contrastive objective to pull matching image–EEG pairs together in feature space, augmented by attention modules to capture spatial correlations and extensive analyses across temporal, spatial, spectral, and semantic EEG dimensions. Evaluated on a large EEG–image dataset, the approach achieves substantially above-chance zero-shot recognition (15.6% top-1, 42.8% top-5 on 200-way tasks) and offers biologically plausible insights for neural decoding and BCI applications.

args.text: Federated EF-Subspace: leverage the empirical low-rank structure of gradients to design a contractive, curvature-aware compressor within the EF-BV framework. The server maintains a streaming PCA dictionary learned from tiny client-side sketches; each client projects its gradient onto the shared r-dimensional subspace and transmits only coefficients while error feedback tracks and corrects the residual, optionally augmenting with a small client-specific subspace to handle heterogeneity. Under a spiked covariance model where the top-r components capture 1−δ of gradient energy across clients, the induced compressor’s contraction factor scales with δ, so EF-BV yields linear convergence with tighter constants than top-k/random-k and communication that is O(r) per round. This unifies subspace reuse and error-feedback, aiming to outperform LBGM and classical sparsifiers in both theory and practice.

result.text: The paper addresses improving adversarial training for deep neural networks by studying how well the inner maximization (adversarial example generation) must be solved to yield robust models. The key insight is that a quantitative measure—First-Order Stationary Condition for constrained optimization (FOSC)—can assess the convergence quality of generated adversarial examples, and that high-quality (well-converged) adversarial examples are more important later in training but can be unnecessary or harmful early on. The authors therefore propose a dynamic training strategy that gradually increases the required convergence quality of inner-loop adversarial attacks over training, and they support this method with theoretical analysis and empirical results showing substantially improved robustness compared to fixed-strength PGD adversarial training.

result.text: The paper tackles the fragility of current LLM safety alignment, noting that simple attacks or benign fine-tuning can often "jailbreak" models. The key insight is that many failures stem from shallow safety alignment: alignment procedures disproportionately modify the model’s output distribution only for the first few tokens, leaving later tokens vulnerable to manipulation via adversarial suffixes, prefilling, decoding tweaks, or further fine-tuning. To diagnose and mitigate this, the authors present case studies and empirical evidence of this shallow effect, explain how it underlies diverse exploits, and demonstrate that deepening alignment—e.g., by regularizing finetuning to constrain updates on initial-token behavior so safety signals persist deeper into generation—improves robustness. They conclude by recommending that future alignment work explicitly enforce persistence of safety across more tokens and propose targeted training objectives to achieve that.

result.text: The paper examines whether practical approximate machine unlearning techniques—designed to comply with data deletion requests—can also remove the effects of poisoned training examples, a desirable property for mitigating data poisoning attacks. The key insight is empirical: across a range of poisoning types (indiscriminate, targeted, and a new Gaussian poisoning attack), model architectures (image classifiers and large language models), and generous compute budgets, existing unlearning methods often fail to erase poisoning effects even when they appear effective by standard metrics. The authors introduce new poisoning-based evaluation metrics to more precisely quantify unlearning efficacy and show that, while some unlearning methods can modestly speed up removal compared to full retraining, they generally provide limited benefit and are not reliable substitutes for retraining unless provable guarantees are developed.

Its key insight is to make triggers input-aware and diverse so that each poisoned input carries a distinct, nonreusable trigger, which defeats trigger-aggregation and verification defenses. The method trains an input-conditioned trigger generator optimized with a diversity loss and a cross-trigger test to enforce nonreusability, then embeds these varied triggers during poisoning so the model learns the backdoor while conventional defenses and inspection tools fail to find a common pattern. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of accurately estimating policy gradients from off-policy data—a setting where bias and variance make statistically efficient estimation particularly challenging in both Markov and non-Markov decision processes. Its key insight is a characterization of the asymptotic lower bound on mean-squared error for any off-policy policy gradient estimator and the observation that prior methods generally fail to attain this bound. Building on this, the authors introduce a nonparametric meta-algorithm that attains the minimax lower bound and enjoys a novel three-way double robustness (so that consistent estimation of any two of three nuisance components suffices), together with practical procedures for estimating those nuisances. They also prove optimization guarantees showing the rate at which following the proposed estimator’s gradient steps approaches a stationary point.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of training GANs with limited real data, where discriminator overfitting prevents the generator from converging and yields poor synthesis quality. The key insight is to reduce discriminator overfitting not by external augmentations or heavy regularization but by adaptively augmenting the real data distribution with the generator’s own samples—intentionally “deceiving” the discriminator so that it must learn more robust decision boundaries. result.text: The paper addresses the gap in vision-language navigation (VLN) where LLM-based agents handle high-level planning but fail to produce affordance-aware low-level motion control in continuous 3D environments. The key insight is to combine foundation models—SAM for visual segmentation, depth and camera intrinsics for geometry, and an LLM for reasoning—so the agent can infer navigable affordances, propose image-space waypoints, and select the best path without needing explicit 3D prediction or task-specific training. AO-Planner implements this by using Visual Affordances Prompting (VAP) to segment visible ground and generate candidate waypoints, a PathAgent that overlays planned paths into the image for holistic reasoning, and a geometry-based conversion from image paths to 3D coordinates for execution; the system works zero-shot and also produces pseudo-labels to train a waypoint predictor that competes with supervised methods. Experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE show substantial zero-shot gains (8.8% SPL) and a learned waypoint model achieving 47% SR, demonstrating an effective bridge between LLM reasoning and continuous motion control.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of degraded multi-task learning performance when independently trained models are merged: merged models exhibit representation bias, meaning their internal feature distributions differ significantly from those of the original single-task models, which harms downstream task accuracy. The key insight is that this discrepancy can be corrected by learning a small, task-specific module that predicts and removes the bias in the merged model’s representations, aligning them with the individual models’ representations without access to task labels or original training data. The proposed method, called Surgery, attaches a lightweight unsupervised module to the merged backbone and trains it to minimize a distance metric between the merged model’s representations (after Surgery) and the corresponding individual model representations, effectively performing representation-level “surgery.” Empirical results show that applying Surgery to state-of-the-art model merging techniques substantially improves multi-task performance.

result.text: The paper addresses one-shot/post-training compression of deep neural networks, where an already-trained model must be pruned and/or quantized accurately using only a small calibration set and without retraining. The key insight is that the Optimal Brain Surgeon (OBS) framework—originally designed for pruning by using second-order (Hessian) information to assess parameter importance—can be efficiently and exactly realized at modern DNN scale and extended to handle weight quantization as well, enabling principled joint treatment of pruning and quantization. Methodologically, the authors derive scalable algorithms to compute and apply OBS-style second-order updates for both removing and discretizing weights, optimizing a local quadratic approximation of the loss to minimize accuracy loss under compression while remaining time- and space-efficient. Empirically, this unified OBS-based approach yields substantially better post-training compression–accuracy trade-offs than prior methods and enables accurate compound pruning-plus-quantization without retraining.

result.text: The paper tackles the inefficiency of FFT-based long convolutions on modern hardware, where poor utilization of matrix-multiply units and high memory I/O make FFT convolutions slower in wall-clock time than optimized Transformers despite their favorable O(N log N) complexity. The key insight is that the FFT can be reframed as a block matrix decomposition that maps naturally onto specialized matrix-multiply units (e.g., tensor cores) and enables kernel fusion, and that sparsity patterns in this decomposition can be exploited to skip work and reduce I/O. The authors introduce FlashFFTConv, which implements the FFT via fused matrix-multiply kernels and two sparse variants—partial convolutions (skipping blocks to prune spatial work) and frequency-sparse convolutions (skipping blocks in the frequency domain)—to save compute and memory; this yields up to ~8× speedups over PyTorch for exact FFTs, substantial end-to-end gains, and model-quality improvements (e.g., better perplexity, GLUE, vision accuracy, and the ability to handle ultra-long DNA sequences).

result.text: The paper addresses the computational inefficiencies of continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) for density estimation and generative modeling, namely costly ODE integration due to complex trajectories and expensive or approximate Jacobian trace computation. The key insight is to regularize the CNF using optimal transport (OT) principles to encourage near-straight trajectories that are cheaper to integrate, and to derive an exact, efficient trace computation whose time complexity matches common stochastic trace estimators. The method, OT-Flow, combines an OT-based regularizer on the neural ODE dynamics with a novel algorithm for exact trace evaluation, yielding models that match state-of-the-art CNF performance while using far fewer parameters and delivering substantial speedups in training (≈8×) and inference (≈24×) across several high-dimensional tasks.

result.text: The paper addresses how to make large language models (LLMs), especially closed‑source black‑box APIs, reliably express uncertainty to support trustworthy decisions; prior approaches needing internal access or fine‑tuning are often infeasible for these models. Its key insight is that black‑box elicitation can be decomposed into three controllable components—verbal confidence prompts, sampling multiple responses, and aggregating consistency—and that human‑inspired prompting plus consistency‑based aggregation can substantially reduce but not eliminate LLM overconfidence, with larger models exhibiting better calibration and failure prediction. The authors implement and benchmark a systematic suite of prompting strategies, sampling schemes, and aggregation methods across five LLMs (including GPT‑4, LLaMA 2 Chat) and diverse datasets, evaluating calibration and failure prediction against white‑box baselines; they show black‑box methods narrow the performance gap (e.g., AUROC improvements toward white‑box 0.605 from 0.522) but still struggle on hard, domain‑expert tasks, highlighting room for future work.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of LLM jailbreaking—attacks that prompt models to produce harmful content—by asking whether prompt-level defenses can provide intrinsic robustness without degrading benign performance. The key insight is that a learned guard prefix, trained adversarially against both malicious and benign prompts, can steer model behavior away from harmful outputs much like adversarial training does for model parameters. The authors propose Prompt Adversarial Tuning (PAT), which optimizes a control prompt attached to user inputs using a mixture of adversarially generated jailbreaks and regular prompts so the prefix neutralizes attacks while preserving utility, and demonstrate that PAT sharply reduces advanced attack success rates to near zero under grey-box and black-box settings with negligible overhead.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of data-free knowledge distillation where a generator synthesizes training samples for a student, but adversarial updates cause large distribution shifts that make the student forget previously learned knowledge. The key insight is to stabilize the synthetic data distribution by maintaining an exponential moving average (EMA) copy of the generator—an ensemble-like, slower-changing version that captures past generator states—so that the student can be trained on both current and historical sample distributions. The proposed Momentum Adversarial Distillation (MAD) method therefore uses samples from the generator and its EMA counterpart to train the student, reducing catastrophic forgetting and overfitting to abrupt generator changes; experiments on six benchmarks including ImageNet and Places365 show MAD outperforms competing DFKD approaches and yields state-of-the-art results in some cases.

result.text: The paper examines whether differentiable simulators—which provide first-order gradients—actually yield better policy gradient estimates than traditional zeroth-order (likelihood-ratio) methods for long-horizon, physically realistic control tasks; it identifies the problem that system properties like stiffness and discontinuities can make first-order estimators biased or high-variance and thus worse in practice. The key insight is that exact simulator gradients are not universally superior: depending on system dynamics and noise, pure first-order estimates can suffer from structural bias or variance issues, so a hybrid that interpolates between zero- and first-order information can capture the best of both worlds. Concretely, the authors analyze bias and variance trade-offs, introduce an α-order gradient estimator parameterized by α∈[0,1] that blends zeroth- and first-order terms to adaptively exploit exact gradients when helpful and fall back to robust zeroth-order behavior otherwise, and validate the approach on numerical examples showing scenarios where traditional estimators fail and the α-estimator improves performance.

Methodologically, ContraD augments discriminator training with a contrastive loss that pulls together differently augmented views of the same example and pushes apart real and fake features, enabling stable training with stronger augmentations and yielding improved FID/IS and linear evaluation performance. result.text: CoDet tackles the challenge of obtaining reliable region-word alignments from image-caption pairs for open-vocabulary object detection, avoiding reliance on pre-aligned vision-language models that can mislocalize or fail to generalize. The key insight is to reframe alignment as a co-occurring object discovery task: images whose captions mention the same concept will contain objects of that concept that repeatedly co-occur across the image group, so discovering visually similar regions across such groups yields robust region-word correspondences. Methodologically, CoDet groups images by shared caption concepts, mines visually similar regions across each group to identify co-occurring objects, and aligns these discovered regions with the concept to train an object detector; this approach scales effectively with larger backbones and achieves state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detection performance on benchmarks like OV-LVIS.

result.text: This paper addresses the lack of interpretability in metaphor identification: prior sequence-tagging approaches detect metaphoricity but do not model the underlying source-to-target concept projections posited by Conceptual Metaphor Theory, so their predictions are unexplainable. result.text: The paper addresses the practical failure modes of Expected Improvement (EI) and its variants in Bayesian optimization, where acquisition values often underflow to zero in many regions as observations, dimensionality, constraints, or parallel evaluations increase, leading to poor and inconsistent optimization performance. The key insight is that these failures are largely numerical rather than conceptual: taking a numerically stable transformation (logarithm) of the EI-style acquisition functions preserves their optima (exactly or approximately) while avoiding vanishing values and other pathologies that hinder optimization algorithms. The authors introduce the LogEI family—log-domain reformulations of EI, Expected Hypervolume Improvement (EHVI), and their constrained, noisy, and parallel extensions—derive analytic and approximate expressions that maintain equivalent maximizers, and implement them within standard optimization routines. Empirically, LogEI variants substantially improve optimization reliability and performance over canonical EI formulations and surprisingly match or surpass several recent state-of-the-art acquisition functions, underscoring the critical role of numerical stability in acquisition optimization.

result.text: The paper tackles video-to-audio generation, aiming to produce high-quality, temporally synchronized audio from silent video while being efficient at sampling. args.text: We propose a joint temporal link-and-time forecaster that routes each query to a mixture of reasoners: a TEKG-based rule-path expert with interval PDFs for when-prediction, a rotation-based embedding expert for who-prediction, and a copy-generation expert to exploit repetition. A contrastive router estimates whether the query is history-driven or novelty-driven and produces per-relation, per-time routing weights; training enforces a consistency loss that aligns the tail-entity likelihood with the rule-induced interval density and adds interval-logic regularization. We further calibrate the router with conformal risk control so that, under cold-start or scarce history, the model defers to rule paths, while in recurrent regimes it shifts toward copy or rotation experts, yielding explainable rationales via selected rules. This joint, uncertainty-aware mixture improves both entity ranking and time-interval MAE on forecasting benchmarks while providing calibrated, interpretable decisions about which temporal signal drives each prediction.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of efficiently approximating second-order (inverse-Hessian) information for deep networks without forming or storing large matrices, enabling practical use in compression and optimization. The key insight is to exploit settings where the Hessian (or its empirical Fisher approximation) is a sum of m rank-one matrices and to derive matrix-free algorithms that compute inverse-Hessian–vector products (IHVPs) with linear dependence on the parameter dimension d and low dependence on m. The authors present M-FAC: one algorithm for pruning that uses O(d m^2) precomputation, O(d m) per IHVP, and O(m) per inverse element query; and a second algorithm for optimization that maintains an IHVP over a sliding window of gradients with O(d m + m^2) IHVP cost and O(d m + m^3) cost to add/remove a gradient. Empirically, these methods achieve state-of-the-art pruning and preconditioned-SGD performance while substantially reducing computational and memory overhead compared to prior second-order approaches.

result.text: The paper tackles the scalability bottleneck of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) training, which is typically restricted to a single GPU and thus cannot handle high-resolution or large-scale scenes; the key insight is that because each Gaussian only contributes to a small, dynamic subset of pixels, training can be distributed by communicating only the required Gaussians to the corresponding pixel partitions and dynamically balancing load. result.text: The paper addresses the lack of systematic evaluation for jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs), noting prior work often focuses narrowly on model vulnerabilities and ignores diverse attack factors and defenses. Its key insight is that jailbreak effectiveness depends on multiple configurable factors at both the target and attack level, so meaningful comparison requires a standardized benchmark that tests attacks against defense-enhanced models. The authors present JailTrickBench, a benchmarking suite that defines eight key factors of jailbreak attacks, implements seven representative attacks, and evaluates them across six defense methods and two datasets in roughly 354 experiments (~55,000 GPU hours) to quantify how different settings influence success rates. By providing a common evaluation framework and open-source code, the work establishes baseline results and highlights the need for standardized assessment of jailbreaks on defended LLMs.

result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of cross-modal alignment in sign language translation (SLT), where the modality gap between continuous sign videos and spoken-language text hinders direct video-to-text translation and prior work often relies on gloss intermediates. Its key insight is to use a conditional variational autoencoder with dual paths—a visual-only prior and a visual+text posterior—tied by two KL divergences so that the encoder is regularized and the posterior distills knowledge into the prior, yielding better cross-modal consistency. The method implements this by training a prior path that predicts text from visual features and a posterior path that reconstructs text from combined visual and textual inputs, enforcing one KL term for C-VAE regularization and a second KL for self-distillation, and further improving integration via a shared Attention Residual Gaussian Distribution that models the posterior’s textual info as a residual to the prior. Experiments on public SLT datasets show the approach reduces representation discrepancy and achieves state-of-the-art translation performance.

result.text: MMBench-Video addresses the gap in evaluating large vision-language models (LVLMs) on realistic, long-form video understanding by creating a benchmark that more fully probes temporal reasoning than traditional VideoQA datasets. args.text: Support-Conditioned Projected PPO (SC-PPO) replaces PPO’s hard clipping with a differentiable per-state projection layer that enforces exact trust regions while conditioning the projection radius on off-policy mismatch and dataset support. Framed as mirror descent, we take an off-policy gradient step and then project the resulting policy onto (i) a KL/Wasserstein divergence ball via closed-form projection for Gaussian policies and (ii) the behavior policy’s estimated support, with the geometry and radius adapted using an off-policyness metric akin to DEON. This yields an off-policy variant that reuses replay without conservative density matching: it inherits Off-Policy PPO’s ability to incorporate off-policy advantages but avoids clipping bias and enjoys STR-style per-step improvement guarantees under partial coverage. The projection layer composes with CUP-style safety projections to respect constraints, targeting improved sample efficiency and robustness on continuous-control benchmarks.

result.text: The paper tackles Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval (ZS-CIR), where models must retrieve images based on a reference image plus a manipulation description across diverse tasks (domain, object, attribute) without task-specific labels. The key insight is that converting the reference image into a context-dependent pseudo-word token tailored to the manipulation intent lets a text-image matching model attend only to description-relevant visual information, yielding more accurate retrieval. To do this, Context-I2W uses an Intent View Selector that learns a dynamic rotation-like mapping to produce a task-specific view of the same image and a Visual Target Extractor that, guided by multiple learnable queries, captures local target regions; these modules jointly produce the pseudo-word token fused with the text prompt for zero-shot retrieval without extra supervision. Empirically, this approach generalizes across four ZS-CIR tasks and improves state-of-the-art performance by 1.88–3.60% over prior best methods.

result.text: The paper tackles overfitting in graph classification when labeled graphs are scarce by leveraging unlabeled data through contrastive self-supervised learning (CSSL). Its key insight is that learning representations by contrasting different augmented views of the same graph teaches encoders to capture invariant, discriminative structure useful for downstream classification without labels. result.text: The paper addresses the problem of optimally solving multiple, correlated graph-level optimization tasks in ML compilers—such as device placement and operator scheduling—where heuristic rules are brittle and prior learned approaches are sample-inefficient and fail to generalize to unseen computation graphs. result.text: The paper addresses the gap between the community standard of "adaptive attacks" for evaluating adversarial defenses and the reality that many such evaluations are incomplete, leaving purported defenses vulnerable. Its key insight is that failures to fully adapt attacks often stem from methodological oversights—such as not modeling the defense's transformations, gradient masking, randomized or non-differentiable components, or incorrect threat models—rather than from genuine robustness, so systematically constructing stronger adaptive strategies can break many published defenses. The authors analyze thirteen recent defenses and distill practical techniques (e.g., white-box modeling of all defense components, gradient estimation or proxy gradients for non-differentiable parts, expectation over transformation for randomness, careful loss/attack selection, and verification-style checks) to craft complete adaptive attacks, demonstrating how to modify attacks to account for each defense’s specifics. Their method is less a single algorithm than a prescriptive evaluation methodology for designing and documenting adaptive attacks so defenses are tested against the strongest feasible adversary.

result.text: The paper tackles dataset distillation, i.e., synthesizing a tiny dataset that preserves the predictive performance of a full dataset, and argues existing methods rely on heuristic alignment objectives rather than principled measures of information preservation. Its key insight is to treat distillation as an information-compression problem and explicitly maximize the mutual information (MI) between real and synthetic datasets, using MI as a well-defined metric for shared information instead of indirect proxies. Methodologically, the authors introduce MIM4DD, which frames MI maximization within a contrastive learning objective by treating same-label real–synthetic sample pairs as positives and different-label pairs as negatives, minimizing a noise-contrastive estimation (NCE) loss on feature maps to obtain a computable lower bound on MI and using this objective as an add-on to update synthetic data. result.text: The paper tackles high-variance and sampling-error issues in policy learning for contact-rich continuous control, where model-free methods suffer from zeroth-order gradient noise and first-order differentiable-simulation approaches incur errors when simulating stiff dynamics like contacts. Its key insight is that much of the gradient error in first-order model-based RL stems from propagating through simulation horizons that include stiff, contact-rich segments, so reducing the effective model horizon to avoid these segments can lower gradient bias/variance and improve learning. The authors propose Adaptive Horizon Actor-Critic (AHAC), which dynamically shortens the model-based rollout horizon during policy optimization to skip or minimize exposure to stiff dynamics while still leveraging low-variance differentiable gradients, integrating this adaptive horizon into an actor-critic training loop and empirically validating faster, more stable learning. Empirical results show AHAC outperforms model-free baselines across locomotion tasks—achieving ~40% higher reward—and scales efficiently to high-dimensional controls with improved wall-clock time.

args.text: We propose Support-Projected Off-Policy Mirror PPO (SPOM-PPO), a policy optimization method that safely reuses replay by combining an off-policy PPO surrogate with mirror-descent trust-region updates implemented as differentiable projection layers and an explicit behavior-support constraint. This jointly enforces bounded update distance and avoids out-of-distribution actions even with heavy replay, enabling CPI/MDPO-like improvement guarantees where off-policy estimation error enters only in higher-order terms. Empirically, SPOM-PPO should retain PPO’s stability while achieving substantial replay-driven sample-efficiency gains on continuous-control benchmarks.

result.text: The paper tackles the gap in performance between multi-agent policy gradient (MAPG) methods and leading value-based multi-agent RL approaches, focusing on challenges like centralized–decentralized mismatch, poor credit assignment, and inefficient off-policy learning. The proposed method, Decomposed Off-Policy (DOP) policy gradients, trains decentralized actors with a centralized decomposed critic that factorizes the joint value into per-agent components, supports both discrete and continuous actions, and is shown theoretically to have sufficient representational capacity for convergence. result.text: The paper tackles detecting training-set backdoor attacks, where poisoned examples cause a learned model to respond to a trigger, and questions whether such examples can be distinguished from benign data. Its key insight is that without prior structural knowledge of the data distribution, backdoor patterns can be indistinguishable from legitimate predictive features—making general-purpose detection impossible—and thus defenses implicitly rely on latent assumptions. Leveraging an alternative, explicit assumption that the backdoor corresponds to the single strongest feature in the training data, the authors formalize this setting and derive a detection primitive and algorithm with theoretical guarantees. Empirically, this method proves effective, and the analysis clarifies which assumptions underpin prior defenses and when they succeed or fail.

result.text: The paper tackles improving meta-transfer learning for tasks that change over time, identifying that Sequential Neural Processes (SNP) underfit when contexts are small and dynamic and that standard attention mechanisms fail to help in this setting. Its key insight is that attention needs an internally maintained, interactively reconstructed “imaginary” context—a recurrent memory that can be updated over time—to effectively summarize limited, evolving task information. Methodologically, the authors introduce Recurrent Memory Reconstruction (RMR), an attention mechanism that recurrently updates and reconstructs a latent memory through interactions with new context, and integrate it into SNP to form Attentive Sequential Neural Processes-RMR (ASNP-RMR), which they show empirically outperforms existing baselines on various sequential/meta-transfer tasks.

args.text: Replace heuristic PUCT-style selection in search with a learned iterative amortized optimizer that approximates the exact solution of the per-node regularized policy optimization. Concretely, train a compact recurrent inference module that, given node statistics and a (possibly sampled) candidate action set, performs a small number of refinement steps to output selection probabilities, distilling from exact-solutions offline and optionally fine-tuning online for domain adaptation. This amortized search policy plugs into MuZero-style planners with sampled actions to handle large or continuous action spaces, and can be interpreted through the I–P lens as learning the improvement operator while the network supplies the projection, yielding a tunable compute–accuracy tradeoff and stronger value estimates. We will evaluate distillation fidelity vs. exact optimizers, search strength and regret under fixed compute, and adaptive halting policies that allocate refinement steps per node based on uncertainty.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of channel pruning for compressing deep neural networks in a way that preserves accuracy while being trainable end-to-end. Its key insight is that the joint behavior of batch normalization and ReLU indicates which feature maps are effectively deactivated, so channels with high probability of being nulled by these successive operations can be pruned; representing pruning decisions as differentiable, per-channel soft masks lets the network explore more architectures and yields stable training. Methodologically, the authors learn continuous masks for each channel that are optimized together with model weights to softly suppress or retain channels based on BN+ReLU statistics, enabling direct identification of a compact model without a separate fine-tuning stage and resulting in superior accuracy/resource trade-offs compared to prior approaches.

The paper addresses how symmetry from neuron weight permutations obscures and complicates finding low-loss connecting curves (mode connectivity) between trained neural networks. Methodologically, the authors introduce a cheap neuron alignment heuristic to approximate the optimal permutation, provide theoretical support that alignment aids connectivity, and empirically validate via proximal alternating minimization that alignment produces locally optimal permutations and enables simple, planar low-loss paths that improve generalization and robustness (including reducing adversarial robustness barriers) between networks.

result.text: The paper tackles embodied visual active learning for semantic segmentation, where a mobile agent in a novel 3D environment must decide which views to request annotations for in order to improve its segmentation performance under realistic, challenging conditions (e.g., clutter, unusual viewpoints, poor illumination). args.text: Current stepwise preference learning from successful/failed tool-use branches treats all negatives equally and uses a static DPO scale, leaving signal untuned by how bad or uncertain a step truly was. We propose Value-Gap DPO for Tools: train a step-value model over partial tool traces via tree rollouts to estimate expected task success and derive margin-weighted preferences whose strengths are proportional to the value gap between the taken and best alternative at each node, then drive DPO with a dynamic, batch-wise beta calibrated from these value/uncertainty statistics. Actively expand the tree where the value model has high uncertainty to harvest the most informative failures, and optionally reuse the value model at inference to prune tool calls. This should yield better generalization to unseen APIs and higher reasoning efficiency than uniform stepwise DPO.

result.text: The paper addresses how to learn accurate predictors when training data contain missing values, questioning the common two-step practice of imputing first and then fitting a predictor. The key insight is that for nearly all imputation functions, an impute-then-regress strategy with a sufficiently flexible learner is asymptotically Bayes-optimal for prediction across any missingness mechanism, so perfect conditional imputation is unnecessary and can even produce discontinuous regression targets that are hard to learn; this motivates jointly learning imputation and prediction instead of treating them as separate problems. Methodologically, the authors adapt NeuMiss—a neural architecture designed to model conditional relationships between observed and missing components under arbitrary missingness patterns—and train it end-to-end to perform imputation and regression together, showing empirically that this joint approach outperforms various two-step procedures on finite-sample experiments.

args.text: We propose Video-to-Stems: a video-conditioned soundtrack generator that jointly models and generates separate musical stems (e.g., drums, bass, melody, ambience) aligned to visual events and long-horizon structure. The method conditions a multi-source joint score model on temporally aligned visual embeddings and rhythm-aware context encoders, while assigning each stem a dedicated cross-attention pathway to instance-tracked visual tokens; training enforces mixture consistency and cross-stem coherence so stems sum to a plausible mix yet remain individually controllable. This enables forward generation, stem-level imputation (e.g., add drums to a silent highlight), and targeted editing by clamping or guiding subsets at inference. We hypothesize this factorized, joint modeling improves rhythmic alignment, semantic correspondence, and editability over single-track V2A baselines, while retaining fast sampling via modern latent/score formulations.

result.text: The paper addresses forecasting and modeling of dynamically evolving (homogeneous and heterogeneous) networks and temporal knowledge graphs, where existing methods treat different network types separately and often fail to capture temporal edge dependencies. Its key insight is to represent nodes by time-evolving latent vectors and model multi-relational interactions with separate, potentially time-varying interaction matrices, embedding both node states and relation mechanisms in a unified latent space whose evolution captures network dynamics and yields interpretable parameters. The method is a Neural Latent Space Model trained with variational inference: at each timestep node embeddings and relation matrices are inferred and allowed to evolve, edges are generated from inner products via interaction matrices, and a variational encoder-decoder framework learns the temporal transitions and performs single- and multi-step link forecasting. Empirical evaluation on homogeneous, bipartite, and heterogeneous real-world networks shows the approach substantially outperforms prior dynamic link prediction baselines.

args.text: We propose Windowed OBS Lookahead, a curvature-aware multi-layer pruning method that bridges first-order lookahead pruning and second-order OBS at DNN scale. The key idea is to use sliding-window, blockwise inverse-Hessian approximations (via efficient IHVPs) to estimate OBS-style loss increases for jointly removing weights across short consecutive layer stacks, yielding a lookahead selection that accounts for cross-layer curvature. Practically, we run a greedy joint pruning within each window while reusing cached IHVPs, and we aggregate per-parameter OBS saliencies into a LAMP-like layer-adaptive rescaling to derive globally consistent layerwise sparsity targets. This enables accurate one-shot/post-training compression and improves high-sparsity regimes versus magnitude/Frobenius proxies on CNNs and Transformers.

args.text: Posterior-Consensus 3DGS trains large scenes by marrying SGLD-based Gaussian sampling with ADMM consensus across spatial blocks: each worker treats Gaussians as samples from a local posterior, proposes births guided by MVS correspondences, runs SGLD steps, and periodically solves an ADMM consensus to reconcile the means and precisions of Gaussians that straddle block boundaries. We place an effective-rank prior on each covariance to discourage needle-like degeneracy during sampling, and perform communication in natural-parameter space (mean/precision and sufficient statistics) with sparse routing of only pixel-relevant Gaussians to shards for scalability. This replaces heuristic clone/split with principled sampling while preserving global coherence, and is expected to improve coverage on textureless regions and robustness to initialization, with lower communication than model-parameter exchange. The approach unifies probabilistic placement, geometry-aware priors, and distributed consensus to scale 3DGS without sacrificing quality.

result.text: The paper tackles offline reinforcement learning, where the challenge is to learn reliable policies from fixed logged data without environment interaction, focusing on avoiding overoptimistic behavior in regions poorly covered by the dataset. Its key insight is to cast model-based offline RL as a two-player zero-sum game in which an adversarial dynamics model is trained to both fit the dataset and minimize the policy’s estimated value, thereby inducing pessimism where the data is scarce. The method, RAMBO, alternates between policy optimization inside the learned model and adversarial model updates that trade off data likelihood with value minimization, yielding a conservative value estimate that provably lower-bounds true performance under PAC-style guarantees. Empirically, RAMBO achieves stronger and more robust performance than prior state-of-the-art offline RL baselines on standard benchmarks.

result.text: Support-Conditioned Projected PPO (SC-PPO) replaces PPO’s hard clipping with a differentiable per-state projection layer that enforces exact trust regions while conditioning the projection radius on off-policy mismatch and dataset support. Framed as mirror descent, we take an off-policy gradient step and then project the resulting policy onto (i) a KL/Wasserstein divergence ball via closed-form projection for Gaussian policies and (ii) the behavior policy’s estimated support, with the geometry and radius adapted using an off-policyness metric akin to DEON. This yields an off-policy variant that reuses replay without conservative density matching: it inherits Off-Policy PPO’s ability to incorporate off-policy advantages but avoids clipping bias and enjoys STR-style per-step improvement guarantees under partial coverage. The projection layer composes with CUP-style safety projections to respect constraints, targeting improved sample efficiency and robustness on continuous-control benchmarks.

args.text: We propose a Process-Window Neural Inverse Lithography Operator (PW-NILO) that composes an FNO-based forward surrogate of imaging+resist physics conditioned on focus/dose and source settings with a DeepONet/FNO inverse head that maps desired wafer contours and process-window descriptors directly to curvilinear masks. The forward surrogate adopts NeurOLight-style unified layout parameterization and masked source encoding to generalize across designs, while the inverse head outputs a SIREN-parameterized implicit mask to capture sharp, sub-wavelength edges under manufacturability priors. Trained end-to-end on LithoBench augmented with synthetic focus/dose sweeps and stochastic perturbations, PW-NILO optimizes across-window fidelity in a single pass and exposes uncertainty via ensemble sampling over process parameters. This enables rapid SMO/ILT co-optimization, replacing iterative simulation loops with a single differentiable operator call.

result.text: The paper addresses novel category discovery: given labeled images for some classes and a larger unlabeled pool containing additional unknown classes, how can one automatically discover and learn those new visual categories without any labels for them. The key insight is that representations bootstrapped solely from labeled data bias clustering of the unlabeled set, so training from scratch with self-supervision on the full dataset avoids that bias while rank-statistics can transfer structured knowledge from known classes to guide clustering of unknown ones. The method trains a joint objective that combines self-supervised representation learning on both labeled and unlabeled images, supervised classification on known classes, and a rank-statistics–based mechanism that aligns similarity ranks from known-class exemplars to induce clusters in the unlabeled data; this combined approach yields substantially improved novel-category discovery on standard benchmarks.

result.text: The paper addresses policy optimization in Markov decision processes where the objective is a general concave utility of the state-action occupancy measure (capturing problems like constrained RL, exploration, and learning from prior experiences), a setting in which the Bellman equation and dynamic programming no longer apply. Its key insight is that the parametrized policy gradient for any concave utility can be expressed via a variational (Fenchel dual) formulation: the policy gradient equals the solution of a stochastic saddle-point problem involving the utility’s dual, which generalizes the classical Policy Gradient Theorem. result.text: We propose Windowed OBS Lookahead, a curvature-aware multi-layer pruning method that bridges first-order lookahead pruning and second-order OBS at DNN scale. The key idea is to use sliding-window, blockwise inverse-Hessian approximations (via efficient IHVPs) to estimate OBS-style loss increases for jointly removing weights across short consecutive layer stacks, yielding a lookahead selection that accounts for cross-layer curvature. Practically, we run a greedy joint pruning within each window while reusing cached IHVPs, and we aggregate per-parameter OBS saliencies into a LAMP-like layer-adaptive rescaling to derive globally consistent layerwise sparsity targets. This enables accurate one-shot/post-training compression and improves high-sparsity regimes versus magnitude/Frobenius proxies on CNNs and Transformers.

args.text: Develop an amortized Fisher-information streaming active learner that replaces per-batch BAIT optimization with a learned recurrent acquisition policy trained to approximate the Fisher-bound objective under streaming constraints. The policy ingests micro-batch features (uncertainty signals, Jacobian sketches for Fisher surrogates) and a compact coreset state, and outputs which points to query to meet a target rate, while a diversity controller maintains coverage via fast submodular-style updates. We train the policy offline with logged streams using contrastive information bounds as a differentiable surrogate for BAIT’s MLE error bound, and online it adapts to distribution drift via lightweight state updates. This yields BAIT-level selection quality with orders-of-magnitude lower compute and practicality in on-the-fly settings, combining amortized design, streaming AL scheduling, and scalable diversification.

result.text: Introduce SCSS-NAS: a differentiable architecture search operator family that unifies kernel size, dilation spacing, and spectral bandwidth by parameterizing convolutions in a continuous form and learning tap locations, while performing mixture selection in the Fourier (and optionally fractional-Fourier) domain. Concretely, we replace DASH’s discrete kernel/dilation options with a FlexConv-style continuous kernel with frequency-controlled bandwidth and a DCLS-style learnable sampling lattice, and search over a small set of spectral and spacing hyper-parameters via weight sharing in the diagonalized domain. To keep the search hardware-efficient, we implement the diagonalization and convolution using FlashFFTConv-style fused matmul kernels, enabling fast end-to-end search and training even at large receptive fields. This yields a compact search space with richer inductive biases for non-stationary signals (e.g., anisotropic textures, PDE fields), where fractional-order angles capture orientation/scale and the learned spacing adapts context range.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of efficient distributed training when devices are heterogeneous and unreliable, where classic high-performance primitives like Ring All-Reduce fail and existing approaches fall back to slower parameter-server or gossip averaging. The key insight is that an iterative “Moshpit All-Reduce” protocol can be designed to perform decentralized averaging with exponential convergence to the global average despite intermittent connectivity and variable bandwidth, enabling near-optimal communication efficiency without requiring a reliable high-speed fabric. Methodologically, the authors derive and analyze this iterative averaging scheme, integrate it into stochastic gradient descent to produce “Moshpit SGD,” prove strong convergence guarantees for the distributed optimization setting, and validate the approach empirically, showing substantial speedups (≈1.3×–1.5×) over competitive gossip strategies on tasks like ResNet-50/ImageNet and ALBERT-large on preemptible nodes.

result.text: The paper addresses the limitation of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), observing that minimizing the perturbed-loss (maximum loss in a neighborhood) does not necessarily prefer flat minima because different curvature directions can yield similarly low perturbed loss. The key insight is to introduce the "surrogate gap," a computable quantity that, for small neighborhood radii, is equivalent to the dominant Hessian eigenvalue at a minimum and therefore directly measures sharpness; minimizing this gap together with the perturbed loss targets regions that are both low-loss and low-sharpness. The proposed method, GSAM, augments SAM with an inexpensive two-step routine—(1) a SAM-like descent to reduce perturbed loss and (2) an ascent (i.e., corrective) step in the gradient-orthogonal direction to explicitly reduce the surrogate gap—yielding provable convergence and improved generalization empirically (notably +3.2% over SAM on ImageNet for ViT-B/32).

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of accurately estimating policy gradients from off-policy data—a setting where bias and variance make statistically efficient estimation particularly challenging in both Markov and non-Markov decision processes. Its key insight is a characterization of the asymptotic lower bound on mean-squared error for any off-policy policy gradient estimator and the observation that prior methods generally fail to attain this bound. Building on this, the authors introduce a nonparametric meta-algorithm that attains the minimax lower bound and enjoys a novel three-way double robustness (so that consistent estimation of any two of three nuisance components suffices), together with practical procedures for estimating those nuisances. They also prove optimization guarantees showing the rate at which following the proposed estimator’s gradient steps approaches a stationary point.

result.text: The paper addresses the security and safety risks introduced when large language models are extended with visual inputs, showing that vision-integrated LLMs create a new, high-dimensional attack surface that can be exploited to bypass alignment guardrails. The key insight is that continuous visual inputs both are easier to perturb adversarially and allow attackers to realize a far broader set of harmful objectives than simple classification attacks, so a single carefully crafted visual adversarial example can universally “jailbreak” an aligned multimodal model. The authors demonstrate this by constructing visual adversarial examples optimized against aligned VLMs (e.g., Flamingo, GPT-4 variants) that, when presented as images, cause the models to ignore safety constraints and follow a wide variety of harmful instructions beyond the narrow training cues used to produce the perturbation. Their results link classical adversarial vulnerability to alignment failures in multimodal models and highlight a fundamental challenge for safe deployment of vision-enabled foundation models.

args.text: We propose Anchor-Needle Provenance (ANP), a training-and-evaluation framework for long-form video LMMs that enforces answer-with-evidence behavior on hour-scale inputs. We plant semantically plausible, multimodal "anchors" (synthetic yet decoupled events) across long videos and pair them with question templates; during training, the model must both answer and return explicit pointers to the referenced segments via learned landmark tokens over temporal blocks, while using hierarchical temporal-window attention to scale. This couples contrastive segment–text alignment with landmark-mediated random access to teach precise referring reasoning and reduce overreliance on world knowledge. We adapt needle-in-a-haystack recipes to the long-video regime and extend referring-reasoning benchmarks with provenance-based scoring (answer correctness plus cited segments), expecting substantial gains in long-video QA and retrieval.

result.text: Support-Conditioned Projected PPO (SC-PPO) replaces PPO’s hard clipping with a differentiable per-state projection layer that enforces exact trust regions while conditioning the projection radius on off-policy mismatch and dataset support. Framed as mirror descent, we take an off-policy gradient step and then project the resulting policy onto (i) a KL/Wasserstein divergence ball via closed-form projection for Gaussian policies and (ii) the behavior policy’s estimated support, with the geometry and radius adapted using an off-policyness metric akin to DEON. This yields an off-policy variant that reuses replay without conservative density matching: it inherits Off-Policy PPO’s ability to incorporate off-policy advantages but avoids clipping bias and enjoys STR-style per-step improvement guarantees under partial coverage. The projection layer composes with CUP-style safety projections to respect constraints, targeting improved sample efficiency and robustness on continuous-control benchmarks.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of poor agent diversity and indistinguishable credit assignments in value decomposition (VD) for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, where existing VD networks produce homogeneous behaviors despite efforts to diversify agent networks. The key insight is that promoting distinguishability at the credit-assignment level—by making temporal credits for different agents more identifiable—will unlock more expressive credit assignments and foster individualistic behaviors that improve cooperation. The authors introduce Contrastive Identity-Aware learning (CIA), which applies contrastive learning to maximize mutual information between agents’ temporal credit vectors and their identity representations, thereby encouraging credit-level discriminability; the CIA module is lightweight, plug-and-play with various VD backbones, and trained alongside standard VD objectives. Empirical results on SMAC benchmarks show that integrating CIA yields superior performance over state-of-the-art VD methods.

args.text: Design-optimized surrogates: instead of training neural operator/graph simulators only for forward accuracy, meta-learn them so that K-step neural-adjoint optimization through the surrogate yields designs that minimize the true PDE objective quickly. The inner loop runs K gradient steps on design parameters using the surrogate (e.g., FNO or a GNS), while the outer loop evaluates the resulting designs with a high-fidelity solver and updates surrogate weights to reduce the real objective and align adjoint sensitivities, directly optimizing time-to-solution. Occasional truth-matching and physics-regularized batches prevent drift and maintain stability under model mismatch, enabling robust, fast inverse design and control across tasks. This reframes surrogate learning from prediction to trajectory-alignment for inverse problems.

result.text: We propose a Process-Window Neural Inverse Lithography Operator (PW-NILO) that composes an FNO-based forward surrogate of imaging+resist physics conditioned on focus/dose and source settings with a DeepONet/FNO inverse head that maps desired wafer contours and process-window descriptors directly to curvilinear masks. The forward surrogate adopts NeurOLight-style unified layout parameterization and masked source encoding to generalize across designs, while the inverse head outputs a SIREN-parameterized implicit mask to capture sharp, sub-wavelength edges under manufacturability priors. Trained end-to-end on LithoBench augmented with synthetic focus/dose sweeps and stochastic perturbations, PW-NILO optimizes across-window fidelity in a single pass and exposes uncertainty via ensemble sampling over process parameters. This enables rapid SMO/ILT co-optimization, replacing iterative simulation loops with a single differentiable operator call.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of detecting post-training backdoor attacks on classifiers when the defender lacks the training data or clean reference models, focusing particularly on challenging two-class settings and cases with multiple simultaneous attacks. The key insight is that reverse-engineered candidate backdoor patterns can be evaluated by an expected transferability (ET) statistic that quantifies how consistently a recovered pattern causes inputs from other classes to be misclassified to the same target, and that this ET score yields a domain- and attack-configuration–agnostic separation between attacked and clean models. The method reverse-engineers potential backdoor patterns from the deployed classifier, computes the ET statistic for these candidates (using the classifier’s responses on held-out inputs rather than any training labels), and flags models as backdoored when ET exceeds a fixed threshold; experiments on six benchmarks show the approach reliably detects both two-class and multi-attack scenarios across different reverse-engineering algorithms.

args.text: We propose a discrepancy-guided curriculum for GAN training that bridges instance selection and fairness-oriented reweighting. First, we warm-start by pruning low-density/outlier real instances in a perceptual feature space to focus learning on the data core; then, as the generator improves, we progressively reintroduce and upweight the real instances exhibiting the highest online per-instance model–data discrepancy. For stability and locality coverage, each reintroduced instance is paired with targeted differentiable augmentations so gradients propagate through transformations in its neighborhood. This closed-loop schedule adaptively allocates capacity across modes, improving fidelity early while explicitly repairing minority/low-density regions later, yielding better precision–recall trade-offs and lower worst-group FID than static filtering or static reweighting.

result.text: This paper tackles image-goal navigation without relying on simulators, reinforcement learning, or ground-truth maps, motivated by the expense and sim-to-real gap of existing methods. The key insight is that passive video of an agent roaming through environments contains sufficient self-supervised signals to learn navigation policies without active interaction or explicit rewards. The method, called No RL, No Simulator (NRNS), trains a policy purely from offline roaming videos using self-supervised objectives that learn correspondences between images and actions (e.g., predicting visual goal-directed progress or relocalization) to guide navigation at test time. NRNS is simple, scalable, and empirically outperforms prior RL-based approaches on image-goal navigation, offering a strong baseline for future work.

result.text: VidChapters-7M tackles the scarcity of large-scale data for segmenting long videos into user-friendly chapters by automatically collecting 817K videos with 7M user-authored chapter boundaries and titles from the web. The key insight is that noisy, scalable user-provided chapters can serve as effective supervision for learning both where chapters occur and what they should be titled, and that pretraining on this large corpus improves downstream dense captioning and localization tasks. The authors formulate three tasks—full chapter generation (segmenting plus titling), title generation given ground-truth boundaries, and title grounding given a title—and benchmark simple baselines and state-of-the-art video–language models, demonstrating that models pretrained on VidChapters-7M transfer well (in zero-shot and fine-tuned settings) to dense video captioning benchmarks and that performance scales with dataset size.

result.text: The paper addresses protecting images from unauthorized use by diffusion-based generative models (e.g., style mimicry or malicious edits) through imperceptible perturbations and asks whether such protections are robust. The key insight is that although perturbations are visually imperceptible, they induce perceptible inconsistencies between the original image and the image reconstructed by diffusion models, and those inconsistencies can be exploited to remove the perturbations. Based on this, the authors propose IMPRESS, a perturbation-purification platform that optimizes reconstructions to minimize the reconstruction inconsistency and thereby purify images, and they use it to comprehensively evaluate and stress-test existing protection methods, showing how purification can weaken their effectiveness.

args.text: Gradient-Guided Consistency Augmentation (GGCA): a per-layer controller for GAN discriminators that continuously estimates the real–fake gradient-norm gap and uses it to (i) adapt augmentation strength/probabilities and (ii) localize consistency losses to feature layers where the gap is largest. In contrast to global ADA/DiffAugment and naive consistency schemes, GGCA selects only margin-preserving transforms and targets to explicitly reduce the measured gap, avoiding artifact-inducing alignment while preserving generator fidelity. To stabilize these localized targets under strong transforms, we add a lightweight feature-quantization head and an instance-contrastive objective that align augmented codes of the same sample yet keep real/fake codes separable, yielding robust, low-variance signals. This unifies adaptive augmentation, gradient-gap regularization, and contrastive/instance-discrimination in a single controller, and we expect significant FID/diversity gains in 1–10k image regimes on CIFAR/FFHQ/LSUN.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem that current vision-language object detectors often ignore rich contextual language descriptions and default to recognizing objects by name, which limits zero-shot detection of novel or fine-grained categories. The key insight is that augmenting supervision with automatically generated commonsense-rich descriptions and training the model with context-sensitive queries forces the detector to attend to descriptive cues (attributes, shapes, relations) rather than rely solely on category labels. The method, DesCo, uses a large language model to expand object names and image captions into rich descriptions and constructs queries that emphasize context, then trains a description-conditioned detector to interpret those queries; this yields substantial improvements on zero-shot LVIS and OminiLabel benchmarks compared to prior state-of-the-art models.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of discovering governing nonlinear partial differential equations from scarce, noisy spatiotemporal measurement data, where existing data-driven PDE discovery methods lack robustness. The key insight is that encoding prior physics knowledge directly into a flexible deep learning model can improve data reconstruction quality from limited noisy observations, enabling more reliable subsequent equation identification. The authors propose a physics-encoded discrete learning framework that trains a convolutional-recurrent neural network embedding known PDE terms, assumed structure, and boundary/initial conditions to reconstruct high-fidelity fields, then applies sparse regression on the reconstructed data to identify the explicit PDE form, and validate this pipeline on three nonlinear PDE systems showing improved performance over baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses Generalized Category Discovery (GCD), where a dataset has both labeled and unlabeled images and the goal is to cluster the unlabeled images into both known and novel classes consistent with the taxonomy implied by the labeled set. The key insight is that existing benchmarks often admit a single natural partition, so models can succeed by unsupervised grouping rather than by extrapolating the labeled taxonomy; to reveal this, the authors introduce Clevr-4, a synthetic dataset with four equally valid mutually orthogonal partitions (shape, texture, color, count) that forces methods to follow the labeled taxonomy. They show strong unsupervised methods fail on Clevr-4 and identify weaknesses in prior GCD algorithms, then propose μGCD, a simple mean-teacher–based method that leverages consistency regularization from representation learning to align unlabeled clustering with the labeled taxonomy; μGCD substantially outperforms baselines on Clevr-4 and achieves state-of-the-art results on the real-data Semantic Shift Benchmark.

result.text: The paper tackles the limitation of current neural architectures that are tied to specific data modalities or tasks and that scale poorly with large, variable-sized inputs and outputs. The key insight is to extend the Perceiver’s latent-based cross-attention bottleneck with a flexible query mechanism that lets the model read from a fixed-size latent representation to produce arbitrary structured outputs, decoupling compute from raw input/output size. Methodologically, Perceiver IO first maps high-dimensional inputs into a small latent array via cross-attention, processes those latents with repeated self-attention blocks, and then decodes outputs by attending from task- or position-specific queries into the latents (allowing linear scaling in input/output size), demonstrating broad applicability across language, vision, multi-modal, multi-task, and reinforcement learning benchmarks.

result.text: Replace heuristic PUCT-style selection in search with a learned iterative amortized optimizer that approximates the exact solution of the per-node regularized policy optimization. Concretely, train a compact recurrent inference module that, given node statistics and a (possibly sampled) candidate action set, performs a small number of refinement steps to output selection probabilities, distilling from exact-solutions offline and optionally fine-tuning online for domain adaptation. This amortized search policy plugs into MuZero-style planners with sampled actions to handle large or continuous action spaces, and can be interpreted through the I–P lens as learning the improvement operator while the network supplies the projection, yielding a tunable compute–accuracy tradeoff and stronger value estimates. We will evaluate distillation fidelity vs. exact optimizers, search strength and regret under fixed compute, and adaptive halting policies that allocate refinement steps per node based on uncertainty.

args.text: We propose Baseline-Matched Sampling (BMS) for policy-gradient RL: decouple data collection from the current policy and actively choose a replay-weighted sampling mixture that cancels baseline-induced bias in the expected natural-gradient direction. Concretely, at each iteration we jointly learn a state-value baseline and sampling-mixture weights by enforcing orthogonality of the control-variate term to the policy score under the target policy, implemented via a three-way doubly robust off-policy gradient estimator with truncated importance weights for stability; the sampling mixture is maintained by a replay-aware entropy-regularized objective. This aligns the estimated update with the intended NPG direction even when baselines alter curvature, yielding on softmax policies O(1/t) convergence as in baseline-stabilized NPG and recovering linear rates with entropy regularization, while empirically improving robustness across baseline choices without extra tuning. The design operationalizes prior insights that baselines shape optimization dynamics and that decoupling sampling restores convergence, while leveraging sample-aware entropy and minimax-optimal off-policy gradient estimation to make the decoupling practical and stable.

We propose a Spectral Tri-Modal Coherence network for short-video misinformation detection that maps video, audio, and text into coordinated frequency-domain representations and diagnoses deviations in cross-modal spectral coherence that signal fabrication, repurposing, or dubbing. Building on frequency-domain fusion for multimodal rumors and inconsistency-aware fusion, we introduce a cross-modal spectral co-selection and phase-alignment module that jointly selects salient bands and measures inter-modal phase/amplitude alignment over synchronized windows. A contrastive curriculum with synthetic perturbations (e.g., audio desynchronization, B‑roll substitution, paraphrased captions) calibrates sensitivity to realistic manipulations while preserving robustness to benign edits. Evaluated on FakeSV with added desync and repurposing annotations, the method targets video-specific artifacts missed by spatial token mixing and yields interpretable band-level inconsistency cues.

I propose PNS-CASTLE: a representation-learning framework that jointly learns a sparse latent DAG and uses necessity-and-sufficiency to gate causal regularization. We discover pseudo-environments and invariant directions in kernel space, estimate feature–target PNS across these environments, and train a feature extractor with a stable differentiable acyclicity constraint while a CASTLE-like reconstruction regularizer is applied only along edges with high PNS. This PNS-weighted graph regularization prunes invariant-yet-insufficient features and anti-causal paths, aligning gradients toward truly stable mechanisms and improving out-of-distribution generalization; when interventional data are available, we incorporate them in the differentiable causal discovery objective to refine PNS and edge orientation. Hypothesis: compared with invariant-risk-minimization or graph-regularized baselines, the method yields lower OOD error and better structural recovery on heterogeneous datasets without environment labels.

result.text: The paper addresses the high computational cost of modern vision-language Transformers and aims to accelerate inference without sacrificing performance. Its key insight is that cross-modal information can guide dynamic token merging during inference—matching and ensemble of visually and textually corresponding tokens yields compact yet informative token sets applicable to both modality-independent and modality-dependent architectures. The proposed CrossGET framework implements this via Cross-Guided Matching and Ensemble, which uses cross-modal signals to pair and combine tokens, and a Complete-Graph Soft Matching algorithm that produces reliable, parallelizable soft correspondences for efficient token aggregation. Extensive experiments across retrieval, reasoning, captioning, and VQA on classic multimodal models and multimodal LLMs show substantial compute savings with preserved or only slightly reduced accuracy.

result.text: The paper addresses 3D object detection on LiDAR point clouds for large-scale outdoor scenes where objects vary widely in scale, requiring both long-range context and fine-grained local detail; prior window-based transformers capture long-range dependencies but tend to blur fine details. The key insight is to divide attention heads into multiple groups that each specialize on a particular spatial range, then merge their outputs to produce mixed-scale features that preserve fine detail while modeling long-range context. The method implements this Mixed-scale Sparse Voxel Transformer (MsSVT) using grouped multi-head windowed attention, a chessboard sampling strategy to cut the 3D windowing computational cost, and sparse voxel sampling/gathering via a hash map for efficiency, yielding a single-stage detector that outperforms state-of-the-art two-stage methods on Waymo.

result.text: The paper addresses the inefficiencies and negative transfer of the Pre-train&Fine-tune paradigm for graph tasks and the lack of standardized evaluation and usability for emerging graph prompt learning approaches, especially in complex and few-shot settings. Its key insight is that graph prompt methods can be unified and fairly compared by categorizing them into two families—prompts as graphs and prompts as tokens—and that a comprehensive benchmark and toolkit are needed to measure their performance, flexibility, and efficiency across diverse conditions. To realize this, the authors build ProG, an open-source benchmark and library that integrates six pre-training schemes and five state-of-the-art graph prompt techniques, evaluates them on fifteen datasets, and provides a unified framework and tooling to streamline execution, objective evaluation, and practical comparison of graph prompt methods.

result.text: Pretrain a scalp-EEG graph encoder by aligning its representations to a frozen intracranial neural foundation model via cross-modal contrastive/distillation, so noninvasive models inherit source-level seizure structure that improves detection and localization. Combine this with self-supervised next-step/masked time–frequency prediction on large unlabeled EEG and montage-perturbation augmentations to learn montage-invariant spatiotemporal features, then fine-tune on scarce labels—expecting stronger cross-center generalization and rare-seizure gains.
